spatial_claims.claim: AB is a straight line divided at C with AC as the greater term and CB the lesser; DE is a rational straight line; rectangle DE by DF equals the square on AB
Point G is placed on segment DF such that rect(DE, DG) = sq(AC) + sq(CB), i.e., DG is the breadth when the rational area is applied to DE
GF is the remaining segment such that rect(DE, GF) = 2*rect(AC, CB), with G between D and F
DG > GF, since sq(AC) + sq(CB) > 2*rect(AC, CB) by 2.7
DG - GF is a positive length with rect(DE, DG - GF) = sq(AC - CB)
DF = DG + GF, so rect(DE, DG + GF) = sq(AC + CB) = sq(AB)
sq(DG) - sq(GF) = rect(DG + GF, DG - GF) via the identity a^2 - b^2 = (a+b)(a-b)

configuration_map: The geometric configuration is minimal and straightforward: points D, G, F are collinear on a line, with G between D and F. DG corresponds to the rational area sq(AC)+sq(CB) applied to the rational line DE, and GF corresponds to the medial area 2*rect(AC,CB) applied to DE. The sum DG+GF = DF corresponds to sq(AB) applied to DE. All remaining reasoning (Steps 7-19) is algebraic, dealing with commensurability relations, rational vs medial classification, and proportions involving ratios of numbers. No auxiliary geometric constructions create competing spatial requirements.
pass_reason: The proof is overwhelmingly algebraic/proportional, dealing with commensurability of areas and lengths in the Book 10 framework. The only spatial content is the collinear arrangement D-G-F on a line, which is trivially consistent: DG + GF = DF follows directly from the area decomposition sq(AB) = sq(AC) + sq(CB) + 2*rect(AC,CB). There are no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, no circle arguments, and no competing spatial requirements from different propositions. All spatial claims are mutually consistent.
